[b]KAMGUSTA's mini Review[/b]

"From the lead of" it is not the same as "from the makers of". Also, it doesn't mean the game will be "as good as".
Short story short, Chet Faliszek, a video game writer who happened to work at Valve, decided to try to earn some more money funding a video game company - this is its debut game. He failed.
Game is unpolished, dull, empty and without a soul. Worst of all, there are no active online servers (even if they advertised so), so you just have to play it with your friends (if you have any) or with bots.
I don't think this game will last - expect it to be abandoned soon.

[b]Recommended buy price 1$
Score 4/10[/b]

This Left 4 Dead clone is completely dead. I've run into a random person just one time, and it kept kicking us due to connection issues.
Also, the AI bots are nearly useless in co-op mode and completely broken in versus mode (they won't even leave the spawn area).
It's a shame because the game has potential but will never be fully realized (unless perhaps there is some sort of f2p model).
A Decent game. It's not Left4Dead so please keep your expectations and comparisons realistic. It's good for what it is.

After getting 4 copies for cheap on a key site, I dragged 3 friends though this dumpster fire. Comparing this game to Left 4 Dead in any way is a travesty. The setting sounds fun but is never expanded on at all, characters are cardboard cutouts. "Barry" (this game's sorry excuse for the Dark Carnival gnome) was never seen once during our playthrough. The zombies feel stiff and samey, the guns feel lame. You'll be getting lost in each level, which isn't good during an escape sequence. The special infected are always a surprise, grabbing/incapacitating/trapping you is often the first thing that tells you they've spawned. Those ones that spawn a pile of spikey balls are seemingly unavoidable, and the Tanks, sorry, Brutes, are easy to evade and are more an annoyance than a threat. The first campaign/episode is the longest, while the rest and half the length often reuse content from that. You never have a clear idea of your goals beyond "go somewhere". Multiplayer is dead, one guy joined us once, and never reacted or spoke, I hope he's in a good place mentally but I strongly doubt it. The final episode is a gauntlet of frustratingly slow opening doors, confusing mazes and a constant stream of boring stiff zombies, which according to the achievements only 1% of players have beat, for good reason, because this game should have a big label saying DROP AND RUN.

In the safe rooms, you can spawn an infinite number of guns from each of the six weapon holders. Me and my friends filled the same room as full as we could until I got <1 FPS, my game crashed and we all had to relaunch. This, as well as spamming the ping button whenever we saw a matter compiler, was our only respite from the 4.5 hours of boring soulless undercooked barely-out-of-Early-Access Unreal Engine crap that is The Anacrusis.

TLDR: Don't.
